items.stem: You paste a Loop component into both a Teams chat and an Outlook email. What happens when someone edits it in Teams?

options.text: The change appears everywhere the component is shared, because it stays in sync
options.rationale: Correct: Loop components are live and sync across the places they are shared.

options.text: Nothing; each paste is an independent static copy
options.rationale: Components are live, not static copies.
The copies stay in sync, not deleted.

options.text: Only the author can ever see the change

items.explanation: Correct: a Loop component is live and stays in sync wherever it is shared.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Microsoft Loop are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Components created in Teams or Outlook are stored as .loop files in OneDrive
options.rationale: Correct: such components are .loop files in the creator's OneDrive.

options.text: Loop is positioned for real-time co-creation, not as an enterprise knowledge base like SharePoint
options.rationale: Correct: Loop is a co-creation layer, not a SharePoint replacement.

options.text: Loop supports the same external sharing and Information Barriers as SharePoint sites
options.rationale: Loop has different external-sharing and Information Barrier behaviour.

options.text: Loop components cannot be edited by anyone but their creator

items.explanation: Correct: Loop components are .loop files in OneDrive and Loop is a co-creation layer, not a SharePoint-grade knowledge base.

items.stem: A shared Loop workspace's owners all leave the company. What happens?

options.text: The workspace becomes ownerless but remains, and an admin can assign a new owner
options.rationale: Correct: ownerless workspaces persist and can be reassigned by an admin.

options.text: It becomes public to the internet
All its components are converted to PDF

items.explanation: Correct: the workspace becomes ownerless, remains in the tenant, and an administrator can assign a new owner.
